title: Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
summary: This sub-technique narrows account establishment to social platforms, where a persona has to survive being looked up by the very people it approaches. The work is mostly cultivation: naming the profile after a plausible real or invented person, borrowing a photo, listing employers and schools that exist, then gradually connecting with genuine users so mutual contacts appear. Adversaries often aim at a specific industry or region, joining groups and reposting content that fits the cover, because a shared interest is what earns a reply. Useful evidence is structural rather than content based: profile age, the growth curve of the connection graph, reused photographs, and the gap between claimed employment and any corroborating record.

beginner.definition: This is the social media version of building a fake identity. The attacker creates a profile that looks like a real person or a real company. They add photos, job details and friends so the profile seems normal. It differs from the wider idea of creating accounts because here all the effort goes into one social platform and the relationships on it.
beginner.whyItMatters: People trust recommendations and connections. A profile that shares your industry and has mutual friends feels safer than an email from nowhere. Attackers use that feeling to start conversations, send job offers or share links. A fake profile can also gather information about your team, your projects and your suppliers. Removing it later is slow, and by then the contact has already been made. Helping staff check profiles reduces the chance of a successful approach.
howItWorks: The attacker picks a target group, such as engineers at a certain kind of company.
They create a profile with a realistic name, photo and employment history.
They post or share content on topics that this group cares about.
They send connection requests to real people, often starting with popular accounts.
Mutual connections appear over time, which makes the profile look vouched for.
They then use that trusted position to start conversations and share links.
beginner.example: Picture a school reunion group on a social site. A new member joins and says they were in your year. They share old class photos and know the names of two teachers. Soon several classmates accept them as a friend. Nobody checks the yearbook, because the story fits and the pictures look right. That is exactly how a fake profile works. It borrows small, checkable-looking details from a real world so nobody feels the need to check the big claim.
takeaways: Shared interests and mutual friends do not prove that a profile is real.
Look at when the profile was created and what it posted before contacting you.
Keep work conversations on company systems where they can be reviewed.

objectives: Explain how a social media persona is built and why it convinces people.
Distinguish this sub-technique from its parent by its focus on social platforms.
Identify profile signals that suggest a fabricated identity.
Describe how a trusted profile is used to approach a target.
Advise colleagues on verifying unexpected social media contact.
